title: Preseason Scouting Report
subtitle: Seven ballots, eight divisions, zero doubles.
intro_paragraphs: Before Week 1 kicked off, all seven of you filed a complete 1-through-4 order for every division — 224 individual predictions locked in before a single snap was played. Nobody's allowed to change their mind now, so here's what the picks actually say about how this pool sees the season, and who's betting hardest against the room.

fun_facts.heading: The Three Locks
fun_facts.body:
Three teams got the exact same fate from every single bettor: the Browns dead last in the AFC North, the Raiders dead last in the AFC West, and the Cardinals dead last in the NFC West. Nobody in this pool is buying a bounce-back season from any of them — seven unanimous last-place votes, three separate times.

There's unanimous ground at the top too: everybody has the Bills first and the Patriots second in the AFC East, the Lions first in the NFC North, and the Rams first in the NFC West. Add the Steelers penciled into third across the board in the AFC North, and that's eight total slots across five divisions where all seven of you agree down to the exact spot.

fun_facts.heading: Most Settled vs. Total Chaos
fun_facts.body:
The AFC North is the closest thing to a solved division — only two different versions of the order exist across all seven ballots, and they disagree on exactly one thing: whether Baltimore or Cincinnati takes first. Everyone has Pittsburgh third and Cleveland fourth no matter what.

The NFC East is the opposite story. Seven bettors, seven completely different orders — not one person matched another person's exact sequence. Nobody trusts this division, and nobody trusts it the same way.

fun_facts.heading: No Two Ballots Match
fun_facts.body: Zoom out to the full 8-division ballot and the pattern holds up: no two people in the pool submitted matching picks across the board. Seven very different bets on the exact same season.

bettor_profiles.bettor-1: Mike T's ballot tracks the room almost everywhere — Ravens, Texans, Bills, Lions, Buccaneers, Eagles and Rams to win their divisions, same as most of the field. The one place he splits off: he's the only person in the pool with the Giants finishing dead last in the NFC East, a division where literally nobody agrees on anything else either.
bettor_profiles.bettor-2: Dilger backs the Bengals over the Ravens in the AFC North — one of only three ballots to do so — and is the lone bettor willing to put the Cowboys in the NFC East basement, in a division where the other six spread their last-place votes elsewhere.
bettor_profiles.bettor-3: Dustin is the most consensus-driven ballot in the pool — not a single pick that stands alone. Broncos over Chiefs, Saints over Bucs, Cowboys atop a chaotic NFC East: every one of those calls has company. If the room is right, Dustin is right.
bettor_profiles.bettor-4: Tom's boldest call carries his whole AFC West bet: the Chargers to win the division outright, a pick nobody else in the pool made — Denver got four first-place votes, Kansas City got two, and Tom is alone on the Chargers. If it hits, it hits big; if it doesn't, there's no consensus to fall back on.
bettor_profiles.bettor-5: Hume is the only person betting against the room's read of the NFC North's back half: everyone else has Chicago second and Minnesota fourth, but Hume flips it — Vikings second, Bears last. Two lone-wolf picks in one division.
bettor_profiles.bettor-6: Cadegn has the most independent streak in the NFC — the only ballot with the Panthers second in the South, the Giants first in the East (over the more popular Eagles and Cowboys), and a full reversal of the NFC West's middle order, with the 49ers ahead of Seattle while six other bettors have it the other way around.
bettor_profiles.bettor-7: Farmer is the pool's biggest contrarian, with six picks nobody else made. Alone on Tennessee third and Indianapolis fourth in the AFC South (six others have Indy third), alone on Miami third and the Jets fourth in the AFC East (six others have the Jets third), and alone on Atlanta second in the NFC South and Philadelphia third in a wide-open NFC East. If this pool has a wild card, it's Farmer's ballot.

closing_paragraph: Locks or long shots, all 224 predictions are frozen now — the leaderboard tracks who's actually right about it, updated every week the season moves.
